Four operatives of the Edo State Security Corps have been arrested for allegedly leaking information about police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City. The suspects, identified as Gideon Acher, Tony Oahiale and Culture Uzo, were arrested while police operatives were tracking suspected cultists in the area. The spokesman for the Edo State Police Command, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operatives were surprised to discover that information about their movements and activities had been leaked. Ikoedem, who spoke during the parade of suspects arrested for various offences, said investigations into the leak led to the arrest of the four security personnel. She added that a separate operation led to the arrest of 10 suspected members of the Aye cult group during an alleged initiation ceremony. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Edo consumer committee rejects NAFDAC warning over product enforcement Traffic grounded as Oyakhilome’s mother’s remains arrive Edo Army foil kidnapping attempt in Kaduna According to her, the four suspected kidnappers were arrested following the rescue of two victims, Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, who were found unharmed during an intensive bush-combing operation in the Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest. She said, “Four personnel of the Edo State Security Corps were arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City. “Others were also arrested for other crimes, which include kidnapping, cultism and armed robbery. “These arrests underscore the Command’s determination to sustain pressure on criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents. “The Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, reiterates the Command’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice. He commends the officers involved for their courage and professionalism and appreciates members of the public for their timely information and continued support. “Residents are urged to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities, as the security of Edo State remains a collective responsibility.” Adeyinka Adedipe
